explain: Trusted request identity is compared with authoritative resource ownership at the service boundary. A caller-supplied owner field cannot grant access.
steps: Load the object from an authoritative fixture. || Check its owner against the authenticated principal before returning its data.
name: ownership

explain: A token acceptance decision requires independently verified signature and expected claims. These booleans model validator outputs; decoding JSON is not signature verification.
steps: Use the result of an established token-verification library for signature status. || Require issuer, audience, and time checks before constructing the principal.
name: jwt-boundary

explain: Cookie attributes, CSRF validation, and CORS are separate controls. This configuration inspection shows that an allowed origin alone cannot authorize a state-changing request.
steps: Describe the cookie attributes as independent settings. || Require a CSRF check for the fixture's credentialed mutation.
name: cookie-controls

explain: ContextVar stores request-local identity and a token restores the prior context. Actual resource authorization is still required in services.
steps: Set a principal for a bounded operation. || Reset it in finally so the previous value is restored even on failure.
name: context-identity

explain: A password-hashing library creates a salted hash, verifies a candidate, and supports rehashing when parameters change. Plaintext and hash values must not be logged; login also needs rate limits and safe failure handling.
steps: Use a compatible argon2-cffi PasswordHasher rather than implementing a hash. || Verify the candidate and check whether the stored hash needs replacement under the current policy.
expect: True with a compatible argon2-cffi installation; the salted hash itself varies and is not printed.
limit: Optional argon2-cffi integration sketch; syntax-checked only. Benchmark the current library policy under your server's concurrency and memory limits before deployment.
name: password-hashing

explain: Request bytes, per-user admission, and tool-call budgets protect different resources. Passing one limit does not waive the others.
steps: Evaluate all three limits for the same task. || Reject before executing expensive work when any required limit fails.
name: layered-limits

explain: Expected business failures use a stable public code and safe message. Internal diagnostic details remain outside the response.
steps: Translate a private failure into an application outcome. || Assert that the serialized public fields do not contain internal connection details.
name: safe-errors

explain: A basic URL policy rejects non-HTTPS and literal private addresses before any fetch. Production SSRF defense must also validate DNS results, every redirect, and network egress.
steps: Parse scheme and hostname rather than searching URL text. || Reject the loopback fixture without making a network request.
name: safe-url
